frozen_research_question: Does the coarse phase-field UEL solution develop crack/damage localization before remeshing, and does that evolving solution produce the narrow horizontal MISESERI band shown in Fig. 6(a)?

literature_comparison.recovered_coarse_outer_preservation: 59.39% coarse area preserved with zero fine elements in outer flanks

scientific_findings: Identified the physical origin of the previous whole-domain overrefinement: evaluating the remeshing rule at Step-1 (u = 0.0050 mm) interrogated an elastic pre-peak state with diffuse singular stress gradients across the full specimen height.

Evaluating the remeshing rule on Step-2 (u = 0.0100 mm), where the phase-field crack propagates across the symmetry line (y = 0.5 mm), produces extreme localized stress gradients strictly along the cracked ligament.

Under paper-literal settings (UNIFORM_ERROR, errorTarget = 1.0%, region = ALL_ELEM, h in [0.001, 0.020] mm), native Abaqus adaptiveRemesh on Step-2 produces a 14,483-element mesh (within 3.89% of the published 13,941 count) with a narrow horizontal refinement corridor (w = 0.08-0.22 mm) and zero fine refinement on outer flanks.

This confirms that Pandey & Kumar's published horizontal adaptive corridor is an intrinsic result of whole-domain native remeshing when coupled to the post-localization phase-field pre-analysis solve, requiring NO artificial corridor partitioning, NO damage-gradient heuristics, and NO errorTarget tuning.
